title: Katz: IDF Told to Prepare 'All-Out War' on PA Officials if West Bank October 7-Style Attack Looms
detail: Defense Minister Israel Katz said Monday, September 7, 2026 that if Israel determines the Palestinian Authority's security apparatus is launching, or about to launch, 'an October 7-style terrorist attack' from the West Bank, he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have instructed the IDF to prepare an 'all-out war' against senior PA officials — including targeting PA leadership, evacuating residents from attack-origin areas, destroying terrorist infrastructure, and maintaining an open-ended IDF presence. Katz said Israel 'will not permit a repeat of the intifada cycle.' The statement followed a stabbing attack at Maoz Yehuda Farm near Kusra that wounded one person, and came alongside IDF readiness exercises (including 'Dawn 2.0') testing multi-front preparedness for an October 7-style scenario. The same day, a joint poll by the Jerusalem Center for Foreign Affairs and Security (JCFA) and Lazar Research — surveying 703 respondents September 2-4, 2026 — found 77% of all Israelis, including 86% of Jewish Israelis, fear a potential October 7-style attack originating from the West Bank; the same poll found 67% of all Israelis (75% of Jewish Israelis) oppose establishing a Palestinian state along 1967 borders.

media.caption: Defense Minister Israel Katz warns of an 'all-out war' on PA officials over West Bank October 7-style attack risk

title: Ofer Winter Defies Netanyahu, Submits Independent 'Amcha Yisrael' Slate Framed Around October 7 Accountability
detail: Brig. Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter submitted his 'Amcha Yisrael' party's 18-candidate Knesset slate to Election Committee Chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg on Monday, September 7, 2026, rejecting days of pressure from Prime Minister Netanyahu and Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich to merge with Smotrich's Religious Zionist Party. The slate — led by Winter, Arab-Israeli activist Yoseph Haddad, journalist Netali Shem Tov, jurist Eran Ben Ari, former Jerusalem deputy mayor Fleur Hassan-Nahoum, and bereaved mother Lali Deri — was explicitly framed around recruiting candidates 'who were not part of the events that led us to October 7,' continuing Winter's campaign message that three years without a state commission of inquiry disqualifies the current political class. Smotrich called the move an 'irresponsible gamble' with right-wing governance; Winter's party rejected 'intimidation' and said it would not unite with parties tied to the pre-October 7 political and security establishment. Polling cited by Israeli outlets suggests the new party could win 4-5 Knesset seats in the October 27, 2026 election.

media.caption: Ofer Winter submits the Amcha Yisrael party's independent Knesset slate, September 7, 2026
